newsitem.title: UK: Next shares squeezed to near-record high.
newsitem.headline: Next shares squeezed to near-record high.

text.p: Shares in Next Plc bounced back to a near-record high on Thursday as renewed buying interest caught some market-makers short of stock, dealers said.
Rebounding from a retreat earlier this week, the fashion retailer was up 19p at 646-1/2 by 0949 GMT in volume of 760,405 shares, just short of its record 649-1/2p set on April 10.
Dealers said Next's move was an example of freqently-volatile nature of the stock.
"It is just Next being Next," said one. "It is a very thin market, it is just a horrible stock to trade."
Next shares, which have more than doubled in value in the past two years, dropped earlier this week, after cautious comment on the stock from analysts at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
The stock received a lift earlier this month from strong results from other retail groups including Oasis Stores Plc.
Elsewhere in the retail sector, Kingfisher Plc was up 9-1/2p at 666 and Marks & Spencer Plc rose 4p at 498.
